top_stories.title: New Passkey Attacks Can Recover Synced Private Keys or Bypass Phishing-Resistant MFA
top_stories.summary: Three separate research efforts have demonstrated attack techniques capable of defeating passkey protections without breaking their underlying cryptography. The attacks involve reusing signed authentication material exposed by Windows, abusing cloud-synced passkey systems via malware, and bypassing phishing-resistant MFA protections.

top_stories.title: Microsoft Entra makes passkeys default as SMS and voice MFA face retirement
top_stories.summary: Microsoft Entra will make passkeys the default authentication method on September 1, 2026, automatically enabling them for users currently relying on SMS or voice MFA. Microsoft-provided SMS and voice MFA will be fully retired on February 1, 2027, requiring administrators to migrate users to alternative authentication methods before that deadline.

top_stories.title: A stranger has been reading Salesforce and ServiceNow portals worldwide for 17 months
top_stories.summary: Researchers at Reco have been tracking a 17-month campaign dubbed "City-Forum" in which an unknown actor has been systematically extracting records from Salesforce and ServiceNow portals globally via a server hosted by a German provider. The attack exploits guest user access configurations in these platforms, making it directly relevant to IAM professionals responsible for managing access controls and guest user permissions.

top_stories.title: Passkey attacks turn Windows logs and Chrome memory into MFA bypass paths
top_stories.summary: Researchers have identified three new attack techniques that bypass passkey-based MFA by exploiting vulnerabilities in Windows event logs, Chrome browser memory, and cloud identity services. Microsoft has patched the Windows logging flaw, but remaining attack vectors involving malware and browser memory extraction continue to pose risks to passkey implementations.

top_stories.title: Microsoft Entra Tenant Governance: multi-tenant administration and drift monitoring
top_stories.summary: Microsoft Entra Tenant Governance has reached general availability, targeting organizations managing multiple Microsoft Entra tenants. The feature combines tenant discovery, cross-tenant delegated administration, configuration monitoring, and controlled creation of add-on capabilities into a unified governance solution.

news.title: The Threat Hiding in Your Hiring Process: How Fake Remote Workers Get In
news.summary: Fake remote workers are exploiting gaps in hiring and onboarding processes to gain unauthorized account access using false identities. Specops Software outlines how document verification and biometric liveness checks can be used to validate that the person receiving access credentials is the legitimate new hire.

news.title: Malicious LiteLLM Releases Tied to Trivy Hack May Have Exposed 2,100+ Organizations
news.summary: Two malicious LiteLLM releases containing credential-stealing code were published to PyPI for approximately 40 minutes in March, capable of harvesting cloud keys, SSH keys, Kubernetes tokens, and database passwords. CloudSEK obtained a dataset of roughly 434,000 captured files indicating potential exposure across 2,100+ organizations.

news.title: Gunra Ransomware Gang Exploits Fortinet Flaws, Bypasses MFA
news.summary: The Gunra ransomware gang is exploiting Fortinet vulnerabilities and bypassing MFA as part of its ransomware-as-a-service operations targeting critical infrastructure. The group leverages leaked Conti ransomware code alongside unpatched flaws in Fortinet firewall and VPN appliances to conduct attacks.

news.title: Researchers Disclose AI-Assisted SharePoint Exploit Chain Reaching Unauthenticated RCE
news.summary: Security researchers disclosed CVE-2026-55040 (CVSS 9.1), an unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability in Microsoft SharePoint Server affecting Subscription Edition, 2019, and 2016 versions. The exploit chain allows attackers to impersonate any user, including administrators, without valid credentials, representing a direct authentication bypass threat.

news.title: Researchers Built a Fake Crypto Startup and Hired Three Suspected North Korean IT Workers
news.summary: Security researchers created a fake cryptocurrency startup and hired three suspected North Korean IT workers as part of an investigative operation. The workers used mismatched identity documents during onboarding, including conflicting state IDs and bank accounts, highlighting fraudulent identity verification weaknesses in remote hiring processes.

news.title: Malicious MCP Servers Can Split Instructions to Make AI Coding Agents Exfiltrate Secrets
news.summary: Researchers have demonstrated that malicious Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers can manipulate AI coding assistants into exfiltrating secrets such as SSH keys and environment variables by splitting harmful instructions into seemingly benign fragments. The attack method bypasses initial refusals by distributing requests across multiple channels the AI assistant already monitors, enabling credential theft without triggering obvious security alerts.

news.title: CaptiveCrunch: Midnight Blizzard Weaponizes Hotel Wi-Fi Captive Portals to Steal Microsoft 365 Credentials
news.summary: Microsoft Threat Intelligence has identified an ongoing credential theft campaign called CaptiveCrunch, attributed to Russian state-sponsored group Midnight Blizzard (APT29), which weaponizes hotel Wi-Fi captive portals to steal Microsoft 365 credentials. The campaign is tracked under cluster Storm-2945 and targets M365 authentication sessions through rogue captive portal interception.

news.title: AWS Secrets Manager adds managed external secrets support for Jenkins and SonarQube
news.summary: AWS Secrets Manager has extended its managed external secrets capability to support automatic rotation of Jenkins API Tokens and SonarQube Tokens. This update allows users to rotate these third-party credentials directly from the AWS console without writing custom rotation code.

news.title: Cisco Secure Access for Government Achieves FedRAMP Certified Class D (High)
news.summary: Cisco Secure Access for Government has achieved FedRAMP Certified Class D (High) authorization, qualifying it for use with sensitive federal data and DoD environments. The certification applies to Cisco's Zero Trust security service, enabling federal agencies to adopt the platform for high-impact workloads under FedRAMP compliance requirements.

news.title: 'GhostJacking' Exposes Identity Governance Gaps in AI Agents
news.summary: New research has identified an attack technique called "GhostJacking" that exploits identity governance gaps in AI agents by manipulating security alerts and blocked events. The attack method demonstrates how threat actors can hijack AI agents through weaknesses in how identity and authorization controls are applied to automated AI systems.

news.title: AWS Identity and Access Management streamlines assignment of IAM roles to workforce users with account access manager
news.summary: AWS IAM launched a new feature called account access manager that streamlines the assignment of IAM roles to workforce users. Administrators can use the feature to assign IAM roles across AWS accounts to workforce users directly from a centralized interface.

news.title: Microsoft unveils Project Perception in July 2026 Security update
news.summary: Microsoft's July 2026 Security update introduces Project Perception, an agentic defense platform that continuously identifies, investigates, and remediates threats. The release includes AI-focused protections specifically covering identities alongside email and cloud agents.

news.title: Microsoft Entra sets November 2026 deadline for memberOf rules
news.summary: Microsoft Entra is retiring the `memberOf` rule operator on November 3, 2026, requiring administrators to update identity policies that rely on this operator. Additional changes include shortened activation times for managed policies and modifications to user re-authentication behavior.

news.title: Microsoft Entra ID will let Windows Hello and macOS PSSO satisfy MFA alone
news.summary: Microsoft Entra ID will update its authentication policies so that Windows Hello for Business and macOS Platform Single Sign-On (PSSO) can satisfy MFA requirements independently, without requiring an additional authentication factor. This change takes effect in October 2026 and affects how organizations configure and enforce MFA policies within Entra ID.

news.title: Microsoft Entra ID is removing an extra MFA hurdle for Windows Hello and macOS PSSO users
news.summary: Microsoft is updating Entra ID to remove an additional MFA verification step for users authenticating via Windows Hello for Business or macOS Platform Single Sign-On. The change will roll out to worldwide and GCC tenants starting early October 2026, with completion expected by late November 2026.

news.title: JVNDB-2026-027667:マイクロソフトのMicrosoft Entra Provisioning Serviceにおけるパストラバーサルの脆弱性
news.summary: A path traversal vulnerability has been identified in Microsoft Entra Provisioning Service, catalogued in the Japanese vulnerability database JVNDB-2026-027667. The flaw affects Microsoft Entra, Microsoft's cloud identity and access management platform.

news.title: Canadian Man Pleads Guilty in Snowflake Extortions
news.summary: Canadian cybercriminal Connor Riley Moucka pleaded guilty to computer fraud and conspiracy charges for hacking and extorting over 165 organizations using Snowflake's cloud data storage platform. The attacks involved stealing data including over 100 million AT&T customer call and text records.

news.title: Device Code Phishing Up 1,500% in 2026; Vishing Doubles
news.summary: Device code phishing attacks have increased 1,500% in 2026, with vishing attacks doubling, as attackers use newer social engineering techniques to bypass security controls. Device code phishing exploits the OAuth device authorization flow, allowing attackers to hijack authentication tokens and circumvent MFA protections.

news.title: Lessons Learned from CISA’s Recent GitHub Leak
news.summary: CISA released a postmortem report on a data breach in which a contractor accidentally published dozens of internal CISA credentials, including AWS GovCloud keys, to a public GitHub repository for nearly six months. The incident highlights credential management and secrets management failures relevant to IAM and privileged access management practices.

news.title: Scattered Spider Hackers Plead Guilty on Day 1 of Trial
news.summary: Two members of the Scattered Spider cybercrime group pleaded guilty in the UK to charges related to the August 2024 cyberattack on Transport for London. Scattered Spider is known for sophisticated social engineering and identity-based attacks, including SIM swapping and MFA bypass techniques used to compromise corporate accounts.
